reference.title: Network port descriptors
reference.shortdesc: network port descriptors expose network port components as BACnet network port objects. These descriptors will allow network port components to be configured from any BACnet device.

li.p: For each specific link layer (Ethernet, MSTP, IP, SC), dedicated descriptors (for example, BacnetEthernetPortDescriptor, BacnetMstpPortDescriptor) are created when a network port is added and removed when the network port is removed.

For the BACnetNetworkLayer's frozen Ip Port property, a BacnetIpPortDescriptor is only added when the network port is enabled. This prevents creating a BACnet network port object for a network port that might not be used, like when a station uses MSTP or SC only. If you later disable the frozen IP Port and decide it will not be used, you can remove the added descriptor from the local device's export table.
The instance number of these descriptors matches the PortId property of the associated network port and is non-editable.

The name of the descriptor and the BACnet Object Name property are initially set to match the name of the Network Port component. If you decide not to change it, both the descriptor's name and the Object Name property will automatically update whenever the network port is renamed.

To make changes to most properties of the BACnet Network Port over BACnet, the BACnet user needs need to have admin write permissions in the station for the Network Port and its descendant components. However, for specific properties like the IP Address and Subnet Mask, the BACnet user will also need admin permissions for other parts of the station, such as the TcpIpPlatformService.

When you modify some Network Port properties, those changes take place immediately. For most other properties, such as linkSpeed, maxInfoFrames, and maxMaster, the changes are added to pending changes and must be activated before taking effect. Pending changes are stored on the descriptor's Pending Changes component. Some properties can be activated by simply disabling and re-enabling the network port. Other properties, such as IP Address and Subnet Mask, can only be activated by rebooting the platform. To activate these pending changes in , you can use the Activate Changes action on the Network Port descriptor.
If you work through BACnet, you can activate changes by executing the Reinitialize Device service, using either the Warm Start or Activate Changes commands.
